latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Honor killings and blood feuds in the North Caucasus, crimes the Soviet authorities tried to wipe out as “survivals of the past,” remain major problems and even appear to have increased significantly since 1991 despite claims to the contrary by local officials.



Exactly how much they have gone up, however, is difficult to say because of the lack of data. A Dagestani scholar’s suggestion that laws should be softened concerning them, however, has provoked a widespread discussion that has brought far more evidence to light.



This information now available underscores that such killings are deeply rooted in the region as a whole, particularly in its eastern third, and that eliminating or even seriously reducing them back to late Soviet-era levels will require enormous and long-term efforts.
